Your first-night guide

Hi {{ contact.FIRSTNAME | default : "there" }}, your pillows are on their way soon. Here's how to get the most out of them from the very first night, so you're ready when the box arrives.

1
Unpack and fluff
Take both pillows out of the packaging and give them a good shake so the shredded foam spreads evenly. Give them a few hours to fully expand.
2
Set each pillow for its sleeper
Unzip the cover and take out foam until the height fits how you sleep. If you share the bed, set the second pillow for your partner. You don't have to agree on height. Keep spare foam in a bag so you can add it back any time.
3
Pick your side
Cool side up on warm nights. The soft bamboo side up when it's colder. Just flip it.
4
Give it a few nights
Any new pillow takes a little getting used to. Adjust one handful at a time until it feels right.
{% if contact.SLEEPER_TYPE == "Side sleeper" %}
Your starting point: side sleeper
Keep all the foam in for the first night. Too high? Take out one handful at a time.
{% elif contact.SLEEPER_TYPE == "Back sleeper" %}
Your starting point: back sleeper
Take out a few handfuls before the first night. Your neck should feel level, not pushed forward.
{% elif contact.SLEEPER_TYPE == "Stomach sleeper" %}
Your starting point: stomach sleeper
Take out a good part of the foam. A low, soft pillow keeps your head from tilting up.
{% else %}
Finding your height
Side sleepers usually keep the most foam, back sleepers a little less, stomach sleepers the least. Start there and adjust one handful at a time.
{% endif %}

Good to know

The cool side feels cold the moment you lie down, thanks to a fabric with a tested Q-max of 0.26. Like every cool-touch fabric it warms up to your body over time, so flip it for a fresh cool side. The outer covers zip off and can be washed at 40°C / 104°F. Don't wash the foam itself.

name: fns D1-nurture-why-hot
subject: Why your pillow feels hot
preview: It's not you. It's what's inside your pillow.
html:
It's not you. It's what's inside your pillow.͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ 
100-night trial  ·  Free shipping  ·  2-year warranty

Why your pillow feels hot

Hi {{ contact.FIRSTNAME | default : "there" }}, if you flip your pillow in the middle of the night looking for the cold side, you're not alone. Here's what's usually going on.

Solid foam holds on to heat

A solid block of memory foam molds around your head, which feels nice, but it also leaves the air nowhere to go. Heat builds up and stays there.

The fabric matters too

Most pillowcases warm up to your skin temperature within minutes. A cool-touch fabric pulls heat away faster, so it feels cool when you lie down.

What we did differently

Our filling is shredded memory foam, so air moves between the pieces. The cool side is a fabric with a tested Q-max of 0.26. And when that side warms up, you just flip it.

5 ways to sleep cooler tonight

Hi {{ contact.FIRSTNAME | default : "there" }}, a cool pillow helps, but your whole bed and bedroom play a part. Here are five simple things to try.

1
Keep the bedroom cool
Open a window or run a fan an hour before bed so the room has time to cool down.
2
Close the curtains during the day
Keeping the sun out keeps the heat out.
3
Choose breathable sheets
Cotton or bamboo breathe better than synthetic fabrics.
4
Go lighter on top
A heavy comforter traps heat. A lighter one is often enough on warm nights.
5
Flip your pillow
Literally. A cool-touch side gives you a fresh, cool surface whenever you need it.
